hypothesis: A stacking corrector that receives the champion portfolio's own cross-fitted logit as an input feature learns where the portfolio is wrong (hard pairs) while reproducing it on easy rows (protect-easy by construction, not by gating); its equal-logit blend with the portfolio reference beats the reference by >= +5e-5 AUC on fold-0 with Spearman < 0.995.
why_distinct_from_prior_negatives: H19-A reweighted training by covariate-locatable difficulty (INC, net ~0). ENS74 reweighted training by portfolio margin |p-0.5| (NEGATIVE, blend below portfolio, but strongest standalone member of phase 20 at 0.961113). ENS75 uses NEITHER reweighting: uniform training weights, and the portfolio opinion enters as an input FEATURE (stacking/residual correction). Deployment is full-vector (no gating) so the candidate differs from the portfolio on every row and the corr limb remains mechanically passable. Row 75 next_action: 'distinct from H19-A fixed reweight; must not degrade easy pairs' -- easy pairs are protected by the model's ability to learn near-zero corrections when the portfolio is already right.
